We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (aniline attached to phenyl). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide formation: product = amide, precursors: carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Wait the amide is attached to the phenyl ring (c3ccccc3N) as an aniline (para? Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline ring). The acid side is the unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group via a phenyl ring: /C=C/C(=O)N... Actually the target: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group via a phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The unsaturated acid is part of the side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N... So the acid precursor would be the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid: c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2? Wait the amide formation uses carboxylic acid and amine. The acid is the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl sulfonyl group: the acid is c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group? Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the first phenyl ring (para-methyl phenyl). The sulfonamide attaches to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). So the sulfonamide formation is between an amine (the first phenyl ring with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl ring? Let's parse: target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have a methyl phenyl (para methyl) attached to NS(=O)(=O) linking to second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). So sulfonamide formation: amine (para-methyl aniline) reacts with sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated acid side chain. So disconnection: break sulfonamide bond to give amine (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl acid?) The sulfonyl chloride would be derived from the second phenyl ring with sulfonyl chloride attached to it (ClS(=O)(=O)-c2...). So we need a sulfonyl chloride precursor.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

Step 1 (final forward): target formed by sulfonamide formation between amine A (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride B (ClS(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). So retrosynthetic disconnection: target -> amine A + sulfonyl chloride B.

Step 2: sulfonyl chloride B derived from sulfonic acid (or sulfonyl chloride) from phenyl ring with side chain. Could be obtained by chlorination of sulfonic acid. But we can consider that sulfonyl chloride can be made from sulfonic acid (SO3H) via SOCl2. So we could have sulfonic acid precursor C: HO-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2. That could be made by sulfonation of the phenyl ring (electrophilic aromatic substitution) but not needed. For simplicity, we can propose that sulfonyl chloride is commercially available. But we need 3 reactions total, so we need to include amide formation as another step.

Thus after sulfonamide formation, we have sulfonyl chloride B which still contains the unsaturated acid side chain (COOH). The next step is amide formation: the unsaturated acid reacts with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give the amide. So disconnection: B (sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid) -> unsaturated acid D (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 2: amide coupling.

Step 3: unsaturated acid D is formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde E (c2ccc(/C=O)??) and malonic acid. The aldehyde would be the phenyl ring with aldehyde substituent: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (para to sulfonyl). The Doebner modification yields α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl. So we need aldehyde precursor E: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl). The sulfonyl group is attached to that phenyl ring; the aldehyde is on same ring. So the aldehyde precursor is 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring; the aldehyde is also on that ring. So the aldehyde precursor would be 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring via S(=O)2Cl attached to the phenyl. The aldehyde is on the same phenyl ring (para to the sulfonyl). So the aldehyde precursor would be 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(CHO)cc2). Then Doebner modification would convert aldehyde to unsaturated acid while preserving sulfonyl chloride? The Doebner modification uses aldehyde + malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated acid. The sulfonyl chloride may survive? Possibly but we can assume it does.

Thus three steps:

1) Sulfonamide formation: amine (para-methyl aniline) + sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) -> target.

2) Amide formation: unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> sulfonyl chloride with amide? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is unchanged; we need to combine unsaturated acid with aniline to give the amide attached to phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So precursor for step 2 is unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline.

3) Doebner modification: aldehyde (ClS(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) (keeping sulfonyl chloride). So final route: start from aldehyde (sulfonyl chloride aldehyde) and malonic acid to give unsaturated acid (sulfonyl chloride). Then amide coupling with aniline to give sulfonyl chloride amide. Then sulfonamide formation with para-methyl aniline to give target.

First, amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Search for functional_groups_broken aliphatic carboxylic acid, formed amide. Already we have templates 133246 and 1593142 etc. Use one of those. Let's pick template_id 133246 (reaction_id 133246). The template ID is not given directly; we have reaction_id and template_hash. The tool expects template_id (string). Probably we can use the reaction_id as ID? The get_template expects template_id. The search result includes reaction_id and template_hash. Not sure which ID to use. Probably template_id is the reaction_id. We'll assume template_id = 133246.

Second, Doebner modification: need template that forms C=C and carboxylic acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. Search for functional_groups_formed "C-C double bonds" and broken "aldehydes" maybe. Let's search.
